thing.text:
PONG, THE ORIGINAL WAY

The game is the green
FIELD, and the ball and the
bat ride on it -- a picture
on a picture. The table is
only the floor it stands on.

A thing riding on a pad has
a place of its own, measured
from that pad's middle, and
its walls are that pad's
edges.

TO PLAY

Set Speed to Instant.

Point at the green PITCH and
press ENTER: the whole board
fills the screen, straight
on, and the workshop gets
out of the way. Escape
comes back.

Then press SPACE: everything
on the pitch starts together.
"." on the pitch stops the
lot.

They keep going until you
stop them -- a behaviour is
switched on and off, not
counted in rounds. The Pause
button in the bar holds the
whole world still.

Move your pointer up and
down: the bat follows. Keep
the ball off the LEFT wall.

Nothing needs clearing away
first. The ball is on the
FIELD, and only what is on
the field is in its way --
not these pads, not your
notebook.

To take the ball or the bat
off the pitch, wake DUSTY
and click it. Clicking Dusty
gives it back, and dropping
it on the green puts it
where you drop it.

THE BALL MOVES ITSELF

It carries a SPEED, the way
the original's did:

  [set | speed | [3/5 | 1/4]]

and then it travels on the
world's clock, smoothly,
whether or not any robot is
doing anything.

So its robots are not
responsible for moving it.
They are left with the only
interesting question: what
to do when it hits something.

FOUR MESSAGES, EIGHT ROBOTS

An EMPTY hole leaves that
one alone, so

  [set | speed | [-3/5 | ]]

means "go left" and says
nothing about up and down.
That is a bounce, in one
message, with no arithmetic
and nothing to flip.

The robots differ only in
the word they expect -- from
the edge reading, or from
the second hole of what it
has run into, which says
WHICH SIDE of the ball the
thing is on.

The original had exactly the
same pair: "Right Collide?"
and "Up Collide?", one
Bounce robot each.
